name: Adoni-Zedek
bio: Adoni-Zedek was the king of Jerusalem. When he heard that Joshua had captured Ai and that the Gibeonites had made peace with Israel, he was greatly afraid, and joined forces with the kings of Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon to form a coalition of five kings against Gibeon, now allied with Israel (Joshua 10:1-5). The Gibeonites appealed to Joshua for help, and Joshua led a surprise night march to their rescue; the LORD sent a great hailstorm on the enemy army and, in answer to Joshua's prayer, made the sun stand still until Israel's victory was complete (Joshua 10:6-14). The five kings fled and hid in a cave at Makkedah; once found, Joshua had his commanders place their feet on the kings' necks before putting them to death and hanging their bodies on five trees until evening (Joshua 10:16-27). Adoni-Zedek's organization of the coalition against Israel and his crushing defeat became one of the defining episodes of Joshua's southern conquest of Canaan.
